title: Heuristic Prefill Negotiator for Speculative Handshake and Safe Fallbacks
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Implement a heuristic-driven prefill negotiator that performs an initial lightweight handshake to select a candidate decode model, emits structured acceptance signals, and provides deterministic safe-fallback behavior when probe acceptance thresholds are not met. This ticket covers design, simulation, runtime adaptor, telemetry, and canary rollout steps. Goal: reduce average latency for short responses by enabling early commit from faster model variants while guaranteeing output correctness via conservative acceptance metrics and a fast fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator exposes a stable API in the runtime to issue prefill probes and receive acceptance signals (proto defined and backwards compatible).
Acceptance metric definitions (confidence, token-level divergence, early-commit score) documented and computed in telemetry.
Implementation includes a fallback circuit that routes to safe model variant under three configurable failure modes: probe-fail, timeout, or low-confidence.
Benchmarks show >=12% average P50 latency reduction for short prompts (<=32 tokens) with less than 0.5% end-user observable quality regression on held-out prompt set.
Canary rollout path automates fallback threshold tuning and includes rollback hooks.
design_notes: Use a two-phase prefill handshake: (1) probe prefill on fast model w/ truncated kv-cache, (2) if acceptance score > threshold, commit and continue decode on fast model; else route to baseline model.
Acceptance score combines: token-softmax entropy delta, prefix-logprob delta vs baseline expectation, and runtime kernel fit heuristic (estimated token-per-second).
Kernel selection info from kernel curator is incorporated into acceptance scoring to avoid misleadingly high confidence on quantized kernels with known bias.
Keep probe payload minimal: sample top-k logits and prefix summary statistics; avoid full token streams to keep probe cheap.
Design a compact backoff policy: immediate soft-fallback (same request re-routed to baseline with preserved kv-cache where possible), and hard-fallback that resets decode state after N retries.
implementation_plan: 1) Spec: finalize probe proto and acceptance signal schema (this ticket).
2) Sim: run offline simulations against Eval prompt set (short+medium) to tune thresholds and compute expected regressions.
3) Runtime: implement negotiator module with pluggable scoring functions and kernel-aware heuristics.
4) Integrate with router: add fast-path rule and fallback circuit; ensure idempotent re-route semantics.
5) Telemetry: add dashboard panels and SLO alerts for miscommits and fallback rate.
6) Canary: staged rollout to 5% traffic by customer tier, automatic rollback on quality/regress alerts.
telemetry: Metrics emitted: negotiator.probe.latency_ms, negotiator.accept_rate, negotiator.fallback_rate, negotiator.commit_divergence_95p
Logs: structured probe events with kernel_signature, model_variant, seed, acceptance_score, decision_reason
Alert: fallback_rate > 2% sustained for 15m triggers pager for oncall runtime-eng
simulation_results: Offline sim on eval-set-v3 (3k prompts): median acceptance score at tuned threshold accepted 48% of probes, P50 latency improved 13.4% for accepted traffic.
Observed small quality shift: measured KL-divergence vs baseline averaged 0.018; human review sample (n=200) flagged 3 items with notable semantic drift.
Kernel-aware variant reduced false accept rate by ~30% compared to score that ignored kernel fingerprint.
risks_mitigation: Risk: false accepts cause incorrect outputs —> Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, mandatory soft-fallback for first 72 hours of rollout per-customer.
Risk: probe overhead increases cost —> Mitigation: probe sampling budget, combine probes across concurrent requests when possible.
Risk: interactions with batching may delay probes —> Mitigation: prefer probe out-of-band scheduler (low-latency queue) and prioritize probe tasks on kernel scheduler.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal QA and dogfooding on staging cluster with synthetic load (1 week).
Phase 1: Canary to 2% production traffic, telemetry-only for first 12h, then enable decisions for next 3 days.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% using automated threshold tuning; monitor user-visible regressions and cost delta.
Phase 3: Full rollout with per-customer opt-out and runtime flag for manual disable.
qa_testing: Unit tests for negotiator scoring functions and kernel fingerprint mapping.
Integration tests: end-to-end request through prefill probe -> accept -> commit and probe-fail -> fallback path.
Load test: sustained 2x peak traffic with probe scheduler enabled to measure latency tail effects.
